name: sap-cdc
_readme: SAP Customer Data Cloud (CDC; products Customer Identity, Customer Consent, CIAM for B2B) as a TARGET only: SaaS with no client code base to scan, so no as_source block and no adapter.py. Built 2026-10-05 for fit/effort estimation of brownfield extensions (a client already runs CDC, usually with SAP Commerce Cloud, in one country and adds a country/site) and as the standard critic's knowledge (standard-sap-cdc). Every non-trivial fact sits in reference-cache.md with URL, date and a verbatim quote verified through the help.sap.com content service; open items are *(verify)* in research-seed.md. Generic product knowledge only.

as_target.default_frontend: CDC screen-sets (UI Builder) embedded in the client storefront via the Web SDK, or CDC Hosted Pages; with SAP Commerce: composable storefront library @spartacus/cdc (Accelerator: gigyaloginaddon, deprecated)

snippets.critic2_persona: seasoned SAP Customer Data Cloud solution architect with several multi-site, multi-country CIAM rollouts behind them, B2C and B2B (Customer Identity, Customer Consent, CIAM for B2B / Delegated Admin), including the SAP Commerce Cloud integration on the Accelerator and on the composable storefront. Knows what the console does out of the box, which features need a separate licence or SAP enablement, and where 'standard' quietly means screen-set JavaScript, a customer-hosted extension endpoint, a webhook consumer or an IdentitySync job. Challenges every 'standard' or 'just configuration' claim by asking: which licence, which site or site group, which data center, which console setting or API, what happens to the existing country, and which verified reference-cache row says so
snippets.docs_domains: help.sap.com: SAP Customer Data Cloud product help (product SAP_CUSTOMER_DATA_CLOUD, deliverable 8b8d6fffe113457094a17701f63e3d6a, version SHIP = current; it includes the full REST and Web SDK reference), the separate 'What's New Viewer for Customer Data Cloud' deliverable, the SAP Commerce Cloud Integration Extension Pack module 'SAP Customer Data Cloud Integration' (product SAP_COMMERCE_INTEGRATIONS) and the composable storefront integration page (product SAP_COMMERCE_COMPOSABLE_STOREFRONT); for adjacent products the SAP Customer Data Platform and SAP Emarsys integration guides on the same portal. help.sap.com is a JavaScript application that answers HTTP 200 for any URL - an HTTP status proves nothing: read pages only through `dbcx safe_web` (which uses the http.svc content service) or `python3 <plugin>/knowledge/platforms/sap-commerce/tools/saphelp.py <topic-url>`, and search with `python3 <plugin>/knowledge/platforms/sap-commerce/tools/sapsearch.py "<generic query>" SAP_CUSTOMER_DATA_CLOUD`. api.sap.com (SAP Business Accelerator Hub) is a single-page app that safe_web cannot read - cite it only for the existence of an API package. community.sap.com only for official SAP product announcements by SAP employees and never as the only source of a reference row. Never use third-party blogs or the open-source Spartacus repository or public npm packages for statements about the composable storefront (a licensed SAP product).
snippets.best_practice: Configuration before code: model sites as a site group with a non-production dummy parent, keep the schema typed (dynamicSchema off, strict validation), create fields only through the Schema Editor, UI Builder or accounts.setSchema and decide name, type and encryption once - they are irreversible; keep screen-sets editable in the UI Builder (Advanced Customization ends that) and put client-side logic into Markup Extensions / screen-set events and the Web SDK configuration of the site group; server-side logic into extensions (customer-hosted, JWS-verified, timeout and fallback policy designed) and asynchronous downstream sync into webhooks (idempotent consumer, return 200 then queue, filter by apiKey in site groups, reconcile with accounts.search after the 3-hour retry window) or IdentitySync dataflows (per-partner quotas); sign every server call with a bearer token or application key, never the partner secret; consent statements versioned per locale on the parent site with a default locale; for SAP Commerce use the Integration Extension Pack module sap-customer-data-cloud (gigya* extensions, Backoffice field mapping per site) and on the composable storefront the @spartacus/cdc library - the Accelerator addons are deprecated; promote configuration with the Copy Configuration Tool for schema, screen-sets and policies and with scripted get/set API calls for the rest.
snippets.critic2_focus: D1: licence and package (Customer Identity, Customer Consent / ECPM, CIAM for B2B, IdentitySync, Data Store, Hosted Pages are separately licensed or enabled), data center (EU1, EU2/Azure, US1, AU1, CN1 ...) and Global Access exclusions (no CIAM for B2B Organization Management, no Data Store, no Flow Builder), deprecations (Accelerator gigya addons, legacy consent solution, legacy lite accounts / Lite preference center, GConnector). D2: is a claimed standard really a console setting or a default screen-set, or screen-set JavaScript / Advanced Customization / extension / webhook consumer / dataflow script. D3: does it work per child site in a site group (most policies, the schema, consent statements, approval workflows and extensions are group-level; children override only a short list) and without regression for the existing country. D4: exact API namespace (accounts.*, accounts.b2b.*, ds.*, idx.*, fidm.*), the documented limits (Acceptable Use Policy rates, search caps, extension timeout, webhook retry window, dataflow quotas) and the SAP Commerce integration path (gigya* extensions, custom OAuth grant, webhook endpoint per base site, @spartacus/cdc).
snippets.effort_rules: Size by mechanism (T-shirt sizes, never person days in a row): (1) console configuration of an existing capability for a new child site (activate site, trusted URLs, policies a child may override, email/SMS templates, screen-set locale, CAPTCHA keys, RBA rules) = XS-S, plus regression testing of the existing country whenever a group-level object changes; (2) new site or site group, CNAME and certificate per root domain, Central Login Page / SSO segment, social apps, permission groups and application keys = S-M including the SAP support tickets' lead time; (3) screen-set work: new fields or locales across every screen-set of the collection, required-field reconciliation on Registration and Registration Completion, consent statements on registration screens = S-M; screen-set JavaScript (Markup Extensions, events, conditional logic, progressive profiling, country-specific age or field rules) = M; (4) extension endpoint (customer-hosted, JWS verification, timeout/fallback, onError UI, hosting and monitoring) = M-L per extension point, more when the code must branch per site; (5) webhook consumer (idempotent, queue, gzip, JWT check, apiKey filter, reconciliation job) = M; adapting existing consumers to a new site's events = S-M; (6) IdentitySync dataflow from a template = S, with custom record.evaluate scripts or a new file/SFTP integration = M; watch the per-partner quotas; (7) user migration of an existing country base (import design, hash algorithm, pending registrations, downstream sync because imports fire no webhooks) = L-XL; (8) CIAM for B2B for a new country in the same site group: reuse Organization Management objects (S), new organization/member attributes, approval paths, B2B templates and Delegated Admin translations (S-M), custom organization registration form, remote approval consumer, ERP/BPID round trip (M-L each); (9) SAP Commerce side per new base site: GigyaConfig + field mapping + session config + OAuth client + B2B webhook in Backoffice/console = S-M; composable @spartacus/cdc configuration per base site = S; anything the integration documents as not supported (cart merge on login, profile update via screen-sets on global sites, refresh tokens, storefront management of B2B units) = custom, M or larger. A requirement that only works with an unlicensed package, a different data center or Global Access plus B2B is an assumption or a blocker, not a size.
snippets.expected_hotspots_d3: country-specific legal texts and consent versions (parent-site statements, per-locale versions, re-consent of existing users), country-specific mandatory fields or minimum age, B2B organisation registration with local fields (fixed screen-set), organisation hierarchies / sub-units (CDC has no nested organizations), approval routing per country, ERP business partner (BPID) round trip, data residency (second data center, Global Access without B2B), cross-domain SSO for a new top-level domain, double opt-in per channel (SMS needs an external verifier), Emarsys / marketing sync per country, migration of an existing user base (password hashes, federated identities), field-level permissions for local service teams, downstream sync of the new site's events
snippets.expected_blockers_d4: Global Access combined with CIAM for B2B Organization Management (not supported), a data center without Hosted Pages, certificate provisioning or the Emarsys connector, irreversible schema / consent / account-model decisions of the existing tenant (field types, encryption, legacy consent solution, legacy vs One Account model fixed per site group), adding an already active site to a group (users lost unless imported; audit log and consent vault lost), Acceptable Use Policy headroom shared across sites (rates, federated sites, app keys, B2B organization cap), per-partner dataflow quotas, extension timeout limits for slow back ends, SAP Commerce integration limits (no cart merge, refresh tokens unsupported, JDK 21 OAuth changes to verify), configuration objects the Copy Configuration Tool does not copy
snippets.content_model_notes: The CDC 'content model' is the screen-set: default screen-sets (Default- prefix, number depends on the licences) rendered by the Web SDK, edited in the UI Builder, localised per locale across every screen-set of a collection, plus Hosted Pages, the Central Login Page, the Delegated Admin console, preference-center pages and email/SMS templates. In a site group the collection, templates and policies are shared unless a child overrides them. A screen-set changed with Advanced Customization can no longer be edited in the UI Builder (also after export). Some screen-sets are fixed: the OrganizationRegistration screen-set (fields and mappings cannot change) and the mobile login screens (no extra input fields). On SAP Commerce, screen-sets render through the GigyaRaasComponent CMS component (Accelerator, deprecated addon) or the @spartacus/cdc library (composable storefront); B2B user management is a redirect to the Delegated Admin console, not a storefront screen.
snippets.api_families_hint: see knowledge target_api_endpoint_families - one REST API per data center (<namespace>.<data center domain>) plus the Web SDK; namespaces accounts.*, accounts.b2b.*, accounts.extensions/webhooks, ds.*, idx.*, fidm.*, socialize.*, audit/reports, SCIM. Default REST responses are HTTP 200 even on error (check errorCode); server calls must be signed (bearer token recommended) or they count against client-side rate limits; limits per API are in the reference cache.
